post.description:
To see which partners AlphaFold DB predicts a protein binds and how confident each interface is. These are predictions from a selective dataset (AlphaFold DB shows NVIDIA complexes only above its own pDockQ2 and ipSAE cut-offs), so a missing partner is not evidence of no interaction, and partners can come from other species: check each partner's organism.

200.description:
Predicted protein complexes in AlphaFold DB that contain a protein, by UniProt accession, entry name, model ID, entry URL or gene symbol and organism; or one complex by its model ID (AF-0000000065932364). Each complex lists its partners (UniProt accession, gene, protein name, organism, copies), assembly, the provider dataset (mostly NVIDIA's proteome-scale homo- and heterodimers), mean pLDDT, the interface scores ipTM, ipSAE, pDockQ, pDockQ2 and LIS, interface_confidence from ipTM (high 0.8 or more, medium 0.6 to 0.8, low under 0.6), links to the mmCIF and PAE image, and its entry page. Sorted by ipTM, highest first; min_iptm filters and limit caps the list. A protein with no predicted complexes returns an empty list.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `complexes` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assembly` | string | homomer or heteromer. |
| `files` | object |  |
| `interface_confidence` | string | From ipTM: high >= 0.8 (confident interface), medium 0.6-0.8 (grey zone), low < 0.6 (likely wrong). |
| `ipsae` | number | Interface score ipSAE, 0 to 1. |
| `iptm` | number | Interface predicted TM-score, 0 to 1. |
| `lis` | number | Local interaction score, 0 to 1. |
| `mean_plddt` | number |  |
| `model_id` | string | AlphaFold DB complex model ID. |
| `name` | string | AlphaFold DB's complex name. |
| `oligomeric_state` | string | e.g. dimer. |
| `partners` | object[] | Chains in the complex with copy numbers; partners can be from another species. |
| `pdockq` | number | pDockQ, 0 to 1. |
| `pdockq2` | number | pDockQ2, 0 to 1. |
| `provider` | string | Dataset that predicted it, e.g. NVIDIA. |
| `source_url` | string | AlphaFold DB entry page. |
| `version` | number |  |

200.description:
The AlphaFold DB predicted structure of one protein, by UniProt accession (P04637), isoform (P04637-2), entry name (P53_HUMAN), AlphaFold model ID (AF-P04637-F1, AF-0000000000710001), alphafold.ebi.ac.uk entry URL, or gene symbol and organism. Returns the model ID, version, date, method and provider, the UniProt residue range it covers, mean pLDDT and the share of residues per confidence band with a one-line reading, confident_regions (pLDDT 70 or more) and disordered_regions (pLDDT under 50) as UniProt residue ranges, whether AlphaMissense data exists, and links to the mmCIF, BinaryCIF, PDB, PAE and per-residue confidence files (coordinates are linked, never returned). Isoform and alternative models of the entry are listed in other_models. Merged UniProt accessions are followed. Unknown or deleted accessions and proteins AlphaFold DB does not model (it covers 16 to 2,700 residues) are not_found with the reason.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| `no_model_reason` | string | Why model is null; null otherwise. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `organism` | object |  |
| `other_models` | object[] | Other single-chain models returned for the same request: isoforms of a canonical accession and alternative predictions, with their mean pLDDT. Call prediction with a model_id for its regions. |

200.description:
AlphaMissense pathogenicity predictions (Google DeepMind) for a human protein, from AlphaFold DB: every possible amino-acid substitution scored 0 to 1 and classed likely benign (under 0.34), ambiguous, or likely pathogenic (over 0.564). Pass variants (R175H, p.Arg175His; up to 50) for their scores and classes, checked against the UniProt canonical sequence. Every call also returns a protein summary: class fractions, mean score and sensitive_regions, the residue ranges whose mean score is above 0.564. Takes the same identifiers as prediction. Canonical human sequences only: other organisms and isoforms are not_found. These are research predictions, not clinical classifications.

The response contains the tool result directly.
